I'm 45, been farming since I was 25 when I married into this village. I only finished primary school, but I know my land. Twenty years on these fields teaches you more than books. I've got 10.1 mu total — about 7 mu I do wheat then maize back-to-back, and the other 3.1 mu I plant cotton. Seven people under my roof: my husband, my in-laws, two kids still at home, and my youngest. We need the wheat for our own flour, the maize for the pigs and chickens, and cotton is what brings cash for school fees and clothes.

It's April now. The wheat I planted last October is greening up. I always plant around October 10th — if you plant too late, the wheat won't survive the winter well. For the wheat, at planting I put down about half a bag of compound fertilizer per mu, that's around 25 kg per mu. Now in spring, I need to topdress. My neighbor Lao Wang's wife said they put down more urea this year because the shop had a sale, but I watch my money. I'll spread about 25 kg of urea per mu at green-up in late March, and if the wheat looks yellow at jointing in April, I'll add another 10 kg. I irrigate three times: now at green-up, once at jointing, and once when the grain is filling in May. Pumping costs money — the well isn't free like the old days — but dry wheat means no harvest. I spray for weeds once and keep an eye out for rust. I expect about 400-450 kg per mu if the weather holds. Harvest will be early June, and there's no time to rest — the maize goes in within a week.

For maize, I buy hybrid seed from the village ag shop every year — saved seed doesn't grow true. That's about 3-4 jin per mu, costs around 60 yuan per mu. We plant around June 12th-15th, right after cutting the wheat. No time to plow deep — we chop the wheat straw and plant directly, or burn it if we're rushed. I put compound fertilizer in the row at planting, about 20 kg per mu, then topdress with urea when the maize is knee-high, about 15 kg per mu. I'll irrigate twice if it's dry — once when the seedlings are small and once at tasseling in August. The maize should give me 450-500 kg per mu by late September.

Cotton goes in around April 20th on my 3.1 mu. Cotton is murder for labor — planting, thinning, pruning, and picking three or four times through September and October. But my mother-in-law and my daughter help with picking, so we manage without hiring too much. I plow and make beds before planting, put down compound fertilizer as base, about 25 kg per mu, then add some urea at flowering. I irrigate three times and spray for bollworm four or five times — that pest will ruin you if you don't watch. I expect about 250-280 kg of seed cotton per mu.

Money is always tight with seven people. I'm spending on seed, fertilizer, diesel for pumping, and some hired labor for harvest when my family can't keep up. I'd rather put a bit more fertilizer than risk a bad year — a failed crop means hungry kids. But I also need cash in hand for emergencies, so I'm not buying the fanciest seed or the most expensive pesticide.
